# Day 27: Parallelised animation function for faster video loading

Date: 2026-03-04

🔧 Technical Wins:
• Separated the frame rendering function into a helper render_frame, which run_animation then calls.
• Used multiprocessing to run the animation logic in parallel cores. This sped up video loading time 2x.
• Tested with 3 workers(cores) instead of 2 but no difference in results. Two workers is optimal for this laptop.

🪛 Next:
For museum demo purposes -
• Add a simple dictionary: DINO_TIMES = {
				"trex":68,
				"triceratops":70,
				"velociraptor":75
}
• Build a Panel grid
• Connect each image to render_time

For optimisation - 
• Cache reconstructed fossil locations for faster compute time. 
  Landmask (for raster colouring), continental_polygons (also raster) & theropods.csv (raw input data from PBDB) 
  have all been cached, but I notice that the fossil locations are being reconstructed every time,
  when it would be more efficient to reconstruct them once, then cache the results and reuse them subsequently.
• Trim whitespace in exported .png images.
• Investigate why exported .mp4 deep-time playbacks have the first 3-5s blank.
